subject: [hw] V33 -> V34: n2shim_log symbol and stderr cell
body:
n2shim_stdio.c defines `void (*n2shim_log)(int prio, const char *tag, const char *text)` (initial NULL) and it is the same symbol __android_log_print should use. prio = Android priorities (2 v,3 d,4 i,5 w,6 e); tag and text NUL-terminated, text is one log line (may contain embedded newlines). stdout (printf/puts/write(1)) uses prio 4 tag "stdout"; stderr (fprintf/err/write(2)) prio 6 tag "stderr". No output happens when the callback is NULL.
Your stderr data cell: I treat FILE* 1 = stdout, 2 = stderr, 3..63 = fopen. So the 4-byte data symbol holding 2 works as is. If a caller passes the ADDRESS of your data cell instead of its value, the runner can call n2shim_stdio_set_stderr_symbol(addr) (exported from n2shim_stdio.c, default 0 = unused). Also available for your exit/abort paths: n2shim_stdio_exit_reason()/exit_status()/exit_pc()/exit_clear() (same file).
